neighbours.label: Archaic second-person speech in dialogue: thou / thee / thy addressed to someone
fire: "Where goest thou at this hour?" the knight asked the stranger.
"I have waited for thee all winter," she whispered to him.
"Thou hast betrayed thy own brother," the king said coldly.
"What wouldst thou have me do now?" asked the servant.
"Get thee gone from my house!" the old woman cried.
"Thy father would be ashamed of thee," the priest said.
"Art thou the one they call the hermit?" the boy asked.
"I give thee my word, and my sword," he swore.
quiet: "Where are we going at this hour?" the knight asked the stranger.
"I have waited for the spring all winter," she whispered to him.
"He has betrayed his own brother," the king said coldly.
"What should we do now?" asked the servant.
"The guests are gone from my house!" the old woman cried.
"Their father would be ashamed of them," the priest said.
"Is he the one they call the hermit?" the boy asked.
"I give my word, and my sword," he swore.
